cover_hook: Overlooked for 100 years, it was a new dinosaur
caption_hook: 🦖 A dinosaur skull sat in a museum drawer for ~100 years. It's a new species, and Europe's 1st megaraptor + 3 more wins 👇
question: Drop a 🦖 if you'd visit the Isle of Wight to hunt fossils
share_line: Send this to the friend who loves dinosaurs
reel_hook: Overlooked for 100 years: a new dinosaur
first_comment: Bonus: its name, Invictibellatrix, means 'unconquered female warrior', chosen to give hope to anyone who is bullied. Love it? 🦖

stories.stat_label: when the museum got the skull
stories.headline: A skull in a museum drawer since 1924 is a new dinosaur
stories.summary: Invictibellatrix amberina, a 3-4 m hunter with claws up to 20 cm, lived 120 million years ago. It is the first megaraptor, a T. rex relative, ever found in Europe.
stories.why: Old museum drawers are still full of brand-new discoveries.

stories.stat_label: villages that will share solar income
stories.headline: 436 Korean villages will share income from their own solar
stories.summary: Residents co-own local solar projects and split the revenue, which pays for higher incomes, welfare and community projects. One region alone now has 125 villages signed up.
stories.why: Clean power that pays villagers directly, not just power companies.

stories.stat_label: years old, a new croc relative
stories.headline: A 170-million-year-old croc relative had needle-thin teeth
stories.summary: Fossils from Morocco's Atlas Mountains revealed Ctenosuchus tenuidens, a long-snouted reptile whose unusually thin teeth suggest it hunted shrimp and small fish.
stories.why: Morocco's rocks keep revealing new branches of the croc family tree.

stories.stat_label: tall, a record for its fungus group
stories.headline: Meet 'D-rex', a giant new fungus that stands 50 cm tall
stories.summary: Found on oak roots in Yunnan's forests, Dianjunus rex weighs up to 2.2 kg, the biggest in its group of 64,000+ species. Its family line began about 65 million years ago.
stories.why: Even giants can hide in plain sight in the world's forests.

fun_fact: D-rex's family arose about 1 million years after the asteroid that ended the dinosaurs.
